predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire (1260-1806)
predecessors.text: the members of 1806 that Cliopatria draws: the founders of 12 July 1806 (Baden, Bavaria, Berg, Hesse-Darmstadt, Württemberg, Regensburg, Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen, Nassau), Würzburg (23 September)…

successors.name: German Confederation
successors.text: 'Most central and southern members survived with minor border changes and formed the German Confederation' (Congress of Vienna, 1814-1815)

rulers.name: Napoleon I, Protector of the Confederation
rulers.title: Protector (hereditary office of the Emperor of the French)

ledger.x: 12 July 1806: German princes found the Confederation of the Rhine in Napoleon's protectorate.
23 September 1806: the Grand Duchy of Würzburg joins (membership table).
11 December 1806: the Kingdom of Saxony joins (membership table).

ledger.cp: Saxon duchies (Coburg, Gotha, Hildburghausen, Meiningen, Weimar)

ledger.x: 11 and 18 April 1807: the small northern and central states join.
ledger.cp: Anhalt, Lippe, Reuss, Schaumburg-Lippe, Schwarzburg and Waldeck

ledger.x: 15 November 1807: the Kingdom of Westphalia joins (membership table).
18 February 1808: Mecklenburg-Strelitz joins; Mecklenburg-Schwerin follows on 22 March 1808 (membership table).
13 December 1810: France annexes Oldenburg and Salm.

wars.name: Battle of Leipzig
wars.outcome: After the battle (19 October 1813) many members changed sides; the allies dissolved the confederation on 4 November 1813.

certainty.note: An association has no frontier of its own; the extent given is the union of the members' Cliopatria outlines, which are approximations, and the pages give no boundary lines.
